zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 7; they obstruct the view downward from Decks 8 and 9, with Deck 8 experiencing the most significant blockage.
zones.effect: You see the horizon and ocean clearly, but looking straight down you see orange fiberglass boat roofs instead of water; Deck 8 cabins sit almost level with the boat tops.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to first-time cruisers or those who want unobstructed water views at all angles; doesn't matter to experienced cruisers who focus on the horizon, or anyone who prefers the steadier ride and lower cost of these decks.

zones.what: The Horizon Court buffet (Lido deck restaurant) operates directly below the midship section of Deck 9 and two decks below midship Deck 10.
zones.effect: Expect noise and foot traffic from early breakfast service (typically 6:00-6:30 AM) through late evening snacks; chairs scraping, dishes, and conversation carry upward.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and anyone sensitive to early-morning noise; doesn't matter if you're up early anyway or sleep soundly.

zones.what: The pool deck, including the main pools, hot tubs, and Movies Under the Stars screen, sits directly above midship and aft Deck 11.
zones.effect: Daytime pool activity, deck chair dragging, and evening movie sound systems operate overhead until 10-11 PM; poolside music and announcements are audible.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for anyone wanting quiet during the day or early evening; doesn't matter if you're out exploring the ship during those hours anyway.

zones.what: The Sports Deck with basketball/volleyball court sits directly above forward and midship Deck 12.
zones.effect: Occasional thumping from sports activities during the day, though usage is typically lighter than pool deck activity.
zones.mattersTo: Minor concern for light sleepers during daytime cabin use; most guests are off the ship or elsewhere during peak sports hours.

zones.what: The Princess Theater (main show lounge) sits directly below Deck 6, with the balcony level of the theater occupying Deck 5.
zones.effect: Evening show sound and vibration from the theater's sound system carry upward, typically 7-10 PM; also pre-show and post-show crowd noise in corridors.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone wanting early-to-bed quiet; doesn't matter if you're attending the shows yourself or are out late anyway.

zones.what: Aft cabins on Decks 5 and 6 sit close to the propulsion machinery spaces.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and hum are noticeable, especially at cruising speed; the motion is steadier here but the mechanical presence is real.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for anyone sensitive to vibration or mechanical noise; doesn't matter to sound sleepers or those who find the hum soothing (some do).

zones.what: Bow thruster operation during docking and tendering creates brief but intense vibration in forward cabins on lower decks.
zones.effect: Loud rumbling for 2-5 minutes during port arrival and departure maneuvers; the anchor chain also runs through this area with metallic grinding sounds early on port mornings.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers who are aboard during early port arrivals; doesn't matter if you're an early riser anyway or sleep through mechanical noise.

zones.what: Primary elevator and stair banks are located forward, midship, and aft on all cabin decks, with midship banks seeing the heaviest traffic.
zones.effect: Cabins near elevator lobbies (typically within 3-4 cabin numbers) experience corridor foot traffic, ding sounds, and conversation from embarkation afternoon through late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those wanting hallway quiet and privacy; doesn't matter to those who prioritize elevator convenience over noise, or who are rarely in the cabin during peak hours.

zones.what: Crew access points to the I-95 crew corridor are concentrated midship on lower decks where crew services (laundry, storage, galley access) connect.
zones.effect: Crew foot traffic in these corridors runs 24 hours, with peak activity during meal prep times (5-7 AM, 4-6 PM) and turnover days; voices and service cart noise carry.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those sensitive to hallway activity at odd hours; less relevant on higher decks where crew access is more limited.
